messages:
elyse: Heads-up — noticed a gap in the console migration where latency histogram buckets import with YAML ends up showing p99 values as if the units were ms but the example was seconds. p50/p95 look fine but p99 reads wrong in the UI. anyone seen this?

sam: ahhh, yep. the shipped YAML example used seconds. the UI import expects milliseconds so it rescales and labels differently. that's the source.

jordan: that also explains the heatmap alignment issue I flagged yesterday. side note: if upstream trace sampling is applied, p99 can look artificially small. we should add a short note about sampling effects.

maria: quick plan: (1) fix the YAML snippet to use ms, (2) add a callout about trace-sampling+percentiles, (3) include a tiny before/after screenshot so reviewers can validate import.

elyse: I'll open a docs PR with those 3 items and tag @sam @jordan for review.

sam: please use this corrected snippet in the docs so copy/paste works: 

```yaml
# latency histogram buckets for console heatmap (units = milliseconds)
latency_histogram_buckets: [1,5,10,25,50,75,100,250,500,1000,2500,5000]
# IMPORTANT: units are ms; previous examples used seconds and break the UI import
```

jordan: wording suggestion for the sampling note: "If upstream trace sampling is enabled, tail percentiles (p99/p999) may appear artificially low. Consider sampling-aware rollups or augmenting with aggregated logs for tail coverage."

elyse: good — I'll add that as a gray callout in the migration guide and inline next to the snippet.

docs-bot: Reminder: PR checklist — include screenshots, cross-links to the trace-sampling page, and run `make docs-preview`.

maria: for screenshots, show both the original (seconds) import and the fixed (ms) import side-by-side so reviewers can see label and value differences. low-effort: reimport into staging and capture two panels.

elyse: I'll add a 2-panel screenshot and a small validation script in the PR description for maintainers to run: 

```bash
# validate that buckets look like ms and are within reasonable bounds
python - <<'PY'
vals = [1,5,10,25,50,75,100,250,500,1000,2500,5000]
assert all(isinstance(v, int) for v in vals), 'non-int bucket found'
assert all(0 < v < 60000 for v in vals), 'bucket out of range (expect ms)'
print('bucket validation: ok')
PY
```

sam: tiny nit: include units explicitly in the YAML comment (you did) and update the docs sample caption to mention units.

elyse: done. Draft PR created: #7432. adding reviewers and the screenshot artifact. pinging infra for a staging import.

deploy-bot: staged import available at https://staging.console.internal/imports/7432-preview — refreshes every 10m.

maria: I'll spot-check the staging import this afternoon and leave QA notes. if clean, merge during a weekday window. :thumbsup:

elyse: thanks all — aiming to merge tomorrow EOD if nothing blocks. will post final PR link once merged.

sam: great catch, thanks Elyse! :raised_hands:
